## What

`iris_doc(mode=put)` reports `success: true` for a document Atelier **refused and did not store**, and returns an `open_uri` naming a document that does not exist.

`do_write` (`crates/iris-agentic-dev-core/src/tools/doc.rs`) decides the outcome from two signals, and neither can see this class of refusal:

1. `!resp.status().is_success()` — the HTTP code
2. `put_body["status"]["errors"]` — the transport-level error array

Atelier answers a refused **document** with a 2xx, an **empty** `status.errors`, and the refusal in `result.status`. That third field is never read.

## Measured

`PUT /api/atelier/v1/USER/doc/{name}` on IRIS for Health 2026.1:

|---|---|---|---|
| created | 201 | `[]` | `""` |
| updated | 200 | `[]` | `""` |
| refused — illegal header line (#16021) | 200 | `[]` | the error |
| refused — no class definition or ROUTINE header (#16022) | 200 | `[]` | the error |
| refused — class name is not the document name (#16023) | **201** | `[]` | the error |

Missing — the script's own comment explains the choice:

Observed against `v0.26.0-interop`. **Not a blocker and not a request** — recording it so it is on
the tracker rather than in a chat log. Whether to add the target is the owner's call.

## The gap

The release matrix (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) publishes five assets:

| platform | arch | asset |
|---|---|---|
| Windows | x64 | `iris-interop-dev-windows-x64.exe` |
| macOS | arm64 | `iris-interop-dev-macos-arm64` |
| macOS | x64 | `iris-interop-dev-macos-x64` |
| Linux | x64 (gnu) | `iris-interop-dev-linux-x64` |
| Linux | x64 (musl) | `iris-interop-dev-linux-x64-musl` |

macOS ships both architectures. **Linux ships x64 only** — there is no
`aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` or `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` asset. So an arm64 Linux host (Graviton,
an arm64 CI runner, a Raspberry-Pi-class box, Docker Desktop's arm64 Linux VMs on an Apple-silicon
Mac) has no asset it can execute.

## Why it is worth a ticket rather than a shrug

This is the third instance of one failure shape, and the previous two were filed and fixed:

- **#174** — the gnu asset links `GLIBC_2.39`, so it downloaded, hash-verified, and then died at
  exec on AL2023 / RHEL 8-9 / Debian 12. Fixed by adding the static musl asset.
- **#423** — macOS published arm64 **only**, so an Intel Mac had no asset at all, and *"the arm64
  file downloads and hash-verifies before failing at exec, which reads as a broken release rather
  than a missing build"*. Fixed by adding `macos-15-intel` and a per-asset architecture guard.
title: no Linux arm64 release asset: an arm64 host downloads the x64 binary, verifies it, and fails at exec

`hook post-edit` takes its **connection** from `.iris-agentic-dev.toml` but its **namespace** from

Verified here by reading, on `b117fdf`:

Sibling of #530, found while fixing it. Not fixed there, on purpose — see below.

## What

`doc_name_with_suffix` (`crates/iris-agentic-dev-core/src/tools/doc.rs`) decides a document's
suffix from its content. For routines it recognises exactly one type:

```rust
return Some(if first_line.replace(' ', "").contains("TYPE=INC") {
    format!("{name}.inc")
} else {
    format!("{name}.mac")
});
```

So `ROUTINE OMORDL [Type=INT]` is stored as `OMORDL.mac`. `.int` is a third routine type, not a
spelling of `.mac`: it is the intermediate code IRIS *generates* from a `.mac`, so a put that
renames one to the other writes a document that the next compile of the real `.mac` can overwrite.

```

  doc.rs:1208   <- the one production caller, the iris_doc mode=put path

  a bare `ROUTINE MyApp.Util`      -> .mac

  no header                         -> None
```

Part of #528. **This is a proposal, to be decided** after the tree-sitter evaluation in the demo project.

## Idea

The server already embeds `tree-sitter-objectscript-routine` (crates/iris-agentic-dev-core/src/tools/symbols_local.rs:597). Today it is used only for label and `#define` symbols.

The routine grammar parses legacy code well:
- dot blocks
- naked references `^(x)`
- indirection
- `LABEL+n`
- `XECUTE`
- `$ZU`
- postconditionals

Measured on the VistA Problem List routines, 0 of 58 files produced parse errors. The only gap seen so far is `$TEXT(+var)`.

- the enclosing routine, label and line
- the **operation**, taken from the parent node: SET target, KILL, LOCK, MERGE, or a read through `$D`, `$O`, `$G`, `$Q` or a plain reference

`parse_int_frame` (crates/iris-agentic-dev-core/src/tools/info.rs:524) accepts a plain routine frame such as `<UNDEFINED>LIST+2^OMORDL` and yields `class = "OMORDL"`. `handle_iris_debug` then:

Part of #528. A sibling of #529; the same script, fixed in the same change.

## What

compile-hook.sh:31-40 builds the document name for a `.cls` as `<parent folder>.<file name>`. **Only one folder level** is used:

| File | Name sent today | Correct name |
|---|---|---|
| `src/OM/API/Customer.cls` | `API.Customer.cls` | `OM.API.Customer.cls` |
| `src/cls/OM/Customer.cls` | `OM.Customer.cls` (right by luck) | `OM.Customer.cls` |
| `src/Customer.cls` holding `Class OM.Customer` | `src.Customer.cls` | `OM.Customer.cls` |

The compile request then names a document that does not exist, which comes back as a 404 that the script reports as a namespace problem, or it names *another* class.

## Proposal

- **Classes:** take the name from the file content (the `Class <Name> Extends …` line), not from the path. Repo layouts vary (`src/cls/Pkg/…`, `src/Pkg/…`, flat).
- **Fallback:** derive the name from the path only when the header cannot be read, and say so in the output.
- **Routines:** take the name and type from the `ROUTINE` header (`[Type=INC]` → `.inc`, `[Type=INT]` → `.int`, otherwise `.mac`), consistent with `iris_doc`.

## Acceptance

Unit tests for:
- a nested package
- a flat layout
- a class name that differs from the path
- a routine with `Type=INC`
- a file with no header, which must be refused rather than given a guessed name
title: compile hook: a class's document name is built from one parent folder, so nested packages compile the wrong document

Part of #528.

## What

`scripts/compile-hook.sh` is registered in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` as a `PostToolUse` hook on `Write|Edit` (plugin.json:33-39). Its job is to compile what the agent just edited, and two defects stop it doing that.

1. **It never uploads the file.** The only request is `POST /api/atelier/v1/{NS}/action/compile` with a document name (compile-hook.sh:57). The file the agent edited on disk is never PUT. IRIS therefore compiles whatever copy it already holds: the *previous* version, or nothing at all if the document is new.
2. **Its verdict never reaches the model.** Every path prints to stdout and exits 0 (compile-hook.sh:27, 60, 67, 81, 99, and the final `echo` at 108/110).
   - For `PostToolUse`, Claude Code shows exit-0 stdout only in the transcript view.
   - The model sees hook output only through **exit code 2** (stderr), or through JSON output: `"decision": "block"` with a `reason`, or `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`.
   - So "Compile errors in X" is printed to nobody, and the agent carries on believing its edit compiled.

Together they make the hook report on a version the agent did not write, to a reader who is not the agent. That is the "a failure answered with a fact" shape this repo's CLAUDE.md describes.

## Smaller things

- **Connection settings come from the environment only** (`IRIS_HOST`, `IRIS_WEB_PORT`… at line 25). The server's own discovery (`.iris-agentic-dev.toml`, workspace file, Server Manager) is bypassed, so the hook

## Why

A demo of Claude Code on **legacy ObjectScript that works directly on routines and globals** is being built on this server. That means:
- `.mac` routines with dot syntax and abbreviated commands
- `$PIECE`-delimited global records and cross-reference globals
- `LOCK` and `TSTART`

Follow-up to #523, which fixes the same defect at `execute_via_generator` step 3. These two sites
read a **single scalar** out of a query reply with `content[0][key]` and default a missing row to a
value that reads as a real answer. Measured shape (see #523): a query that matches no rows answers
HTTP 200 with `status.errors` empty and `result.content` an empty array, so `content[0]` is `null`
and the default fires.

Listed, not fixed, because each default is a *decision* with its own blast radius and neither should
be changed inside a PR about the generator.

- [ ] `tools/info.rs` — the `%Studio.Debugger` capability probe reads
  `COUNT(*) AS N` with `.unwrap_or(0) > 0`, under an outer `Err(_) => false`. A query that fails or
  answers without a row becomes "the method is not available", which is a negative fact about IRIS
  derived from a failure to ask. Four occurrences of the same read.
- [ ] `tools/mod.rs` — the `iris_test` baseline reads `MAX(ID) AS m FROM
  %UnitTest_Result.TestInstance` with `.unwrap_or(0)` and an outer `_ => 0`. A baseline of 0 does
  not mean "no previous results"; it means every historical result now counts as new, which is the
  more dangerous direction for a tool that reports which tests just ran.

Both are probes whose conservative default was chosen deliberately, so the repair is a tri-state
rather than a different default: *answered and the count is 0* is not *could not ask*. Promoting
either changes which error is affordable (cf. the lesson in

body:
`execute_via_generator` step 3 reads the captured output as

```rust
QueryOutcome::Rows(body) => body["result"]["content"][0]["result"]
    .as_str()
    .unwrap_or("")
    .replace('\x01', "\n"),
```

#362 separated the three reply shapes that carry *something to report* — an IRIS error in
`status.errors`, a non-2xx status, a non-JSON body. The shape that carries **nothing at all** is
still read as the empty string, and an empty string from this function is what call sites read as
"the script produced no output".

## Measured

Against a live instance, `POST /api/atelier/v8/<ns>/action/query`:

| query | HTTP | `status.errors` | `result.content` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SELECT 1 AS result WHERE 1=0` | 200 | `[]` | `[]` |
| `SELECT Name AS result FROM %Dictionary.ClassDefinition WHERE Name = 'ZZ.Nope'` | 200 | `[]` | `[]` |
| `SELECT NULL AS result` | 200 | `[]` | `[{"result": ""}]` |
| `SELECT NoSuchFunc() AS result` | 200 | populated (SQLCODE -359) | — |

So `{"status":{"errors":[],"summary":""},"console":[],"result":{"content":[]}}` is a real response
shape, not a hypothetical: `interpret_query_response` classifies it as `Rows` (success, no errors),
then `content[0]` is `null`, `as_str()` is `None`, and `unwrap_or("")` reports it as an empty
output.

Row 3 is the half that makes the repair safe: **a SQL NULL arrives as the empty STRING, not as JSON
null**, so a row that is present always carries a readable value. The empty-value case and the
no-row case are therefore separabl
title: execute_via_generator: a reply that carried no row is read as an empty output

## Summary

In a benchmarked IRIS interop build evaluation driving this MCP through Claude Code, the biggest token sink was **oversized read-tool output that then replays in context on every later model call**. Several read tools can be made much leaner **losslessly** — via opt-out modes, or filters that do not drop any information the model relies on. No change below reduces the information needed for correct code generation.

## Evidence (file:line in this repo)

- **`iris_doc(get)` dumps full raw `.cls` source** — license header + method bodies + verbose `///` comments — even when only the settings / API surface was wanted. `max_bytes` defaults to `0` = unlimited (`doc.rs` ~L610; `handle_get` ~L394–627). Measured: **129 calls / ~182k chars, p90 5.3k, max 12.6k.**
- **`docs_introspect` emits each signature twice** — the raw `FormalSpec` string *and* an expanded `args[]`/`arg_count` array ("strictly additive, FormalSpec left in place", `formal_spec.rs` ~L211–212) — and has **no member/kind/limit filter** (`mod.rs` ~L8229–8242), so it also serializes dozens of unneeded helper methods. Measured: **21 calls / ~148k chars, p90 17.8k, max 25.2k** (HL7ToSDA3 = 17.8k, 13 params serialized twice).
- Lesser offenders: `hl7_schema_inspect` writes empty description/optionality/values + duplicate `type_raw` per field (`hl7_schema.rs` ~L682–692); `iris_compile` / `iris_doc(put,compile)` return the full compiler console even on clean success (`mod.rs` ~L5926–5934, `doc.rs` ~L1886–1892); `
title: Enhancement: skeleton/compact/bounded output modes for the heavy read tools (lossless)
